symptom: On a project whose default language is nl_NL, `create association … on delete restrict error_message '…'` stores ChildErrorMessage as a Texts$Text with only an en_US translation; the app has no message in its language for a refused delete (stored document checked; runtime display not observed). mx check and the build stay green.
cause: deleteErrorText (the leaf behind assocToGen and patchCrossDeleteErrorMessage) built the text with a hardcoded "en_US"; it was added for the runtime-start fix (CapTrackV2 §1) after the #970 sweep moved the other text writers to model.AuthoringLanguage(), so the sweep never saw it. deleteErrorMessageFromGen read en_US first, the mirror image.
insight: A new Texts$Text leaf written after a language sweep reintroduces the hardcoded language; grep for `"en_US"` in writer code is the cheap check. Switching the leaf to model.AuthoringLanguage() is only half the fix: that value is process-level and only set when the executor calls authoringLanguage(ctx), which the association handlers never did, so a backend-only fix passes its backend test and still writes en_US for a script whose first statement is CREATE ASSOCIATION. Assert in an executor test that the language is published before the first domain-model call. Fix the reader with the writer: a project-language writer plus an en_US-first reader turns describe -> exec into an overwrite of the project-language translation.
